note: What each update brings, in plain words for Joshua. One line per change that reaches the Mac, newest last, each with a kind: major (a big change: new major version and a new name), feature (bumps the middle number) or fix (the last number). Keep each line short (under 10 words) and plain: no tech words.

items.text: Your browser is now called Samara.
Only one Samara in your Dock.
Updates get ready in the background. No more freezing.
Each update has a number and a name.
The Update button glows when an update is ready.
Big updates get a new name.
Aang can tell you what each update brought.
Your logins are no longer saved in a sync file.
A new update window with tick boxes.
The Update button changes color the longer you wait.
Skipping an update asks you twice.
You can go back a version, or update overnight.
Check for updates is in Samara's menu.
New lantern icon: lit when open, dark when closed.
The lantern fades on and off smoothly.
Restarting for an update takes seconds.
Claude asks you first before using Samara.
Claude asks before sending your details anywhere.
Web pages can't trick Claude into pressing Send.
AI can never open your bank sites.
Bank sites open in Chrome, with one big button.
Claude can read your tabs, but only if you say yes.
Claude can find hidden job details, like pay.
Shops and PayPal checkouts work as normal.
Claude can't see hidden trick text on pages.
Web pages can't reach your home network.
Mac updates are now signed by your PC.
Mac downloads get Apple's safety check.
More scam sites are blocked, checked daily.
Sites trusted on one computer ask once on the other.
Update tick boxes now glow turquoise.
Click the shield to set each site's rules.
All your site rules, in Settings.
Settings labels are easy to read again.
Claude shows you its plan before it starts.
Untick a site, or tell Claude what to change.
Real job boards like Greenhouse are no longer blocked.
Name a bookmark as you save it.
The popout's see-through icon is just an icon now.
Your Mac remembers Samara's mic permission now.
Netflix on the Mac opens in the paid-video window.
Netflix shows really open in their own window now.
One Samara in your Dock after updates, for good.
Pinned pop-out: the pin lies down and turns gold.
Videos wait for your click; leaving a tab pauses it.
Samara is smoother: quicker tabs, menus and start.
The tab rail slides out carrying its handle.
Pop-out opens fast and fades smoothly.
Claude browses in Samara much faster.
Streaming sign-ins stay on each machine.
Sleeping tabs keep their logos.
Pop-out: unpinned is a normal window; closing pauses.
The tab shows what's playing in the pop-out.
Scroll up on Aang to see everything he showed you.
Undo things you said yes to, right in the history.
Links from Aang open in Samara.
Samara's lantern has a real maple leaf now.
The pop-out has its own turquoise lantern icon.
Samara's taskbar icon is bigger and clearer.
Dragging the pop-out no longer makes it jump.
Samara's desktop icon lights up while it's open.
Samara's taskbar lantern lights up crisply.
Closing the pop-out brings Samara back.
Picking a spelling in the right-click menu works.
Dark mode comes on as pages open, Gmail too.
Right-click: save links, send words to Aang, pop out videos.
Bookmarks are big raised keys with name banners.
Bookmarks sit in a carved frame with gold corners.
Tabs got the same look as bookmarks, easier to read.
Adding a bookmark from the tab list no longer freezes.
Right-click a bookmark: rename, move, remove and more.
Bookmark names always show in full, never cut off.
Going back a version never adds a second Samara to your Dock.
Dark mode is lighter: sites use their own dark look first.
Updates never leave a second Samara in your Dock.
Claude's mockups get their own trail, with every version.
Right-click a mockup to send it to Aang.
Claude can file mockups into a branch.
The one cockpit bubble is built: talk, look back and answer in one place (off until you switch it on).
Aang now hears every Claude session on this PC: its to-do list, and when it needs your yes or an answer.
Briefs, videos and plans now open inside the cockpit.
Claude's questions now come in plain words, and your answers go back clear and precise.
Claude's jobs and questions now live in the cockpit.
Marks over Aang's head and wooden chimes for Claude's work.
Smoother tab dragging: slide right to tuck under.
Each kind of message has its own paper; hover for its label.
A Claude rune in Samara's bar shows job progress.
Aang's chat box holds still and opens small.
Right-click Samara's taskbar icon for shortcuts; rune wears Claude's logo.
Claude job bars move live and say what Claude is doing.
Aang talks in one light speech bubble again.
Hold a Claude job in Aang's bubble to pop it out onto your desktop.
Aang's speech bubble has a slim wooden edge.
Right-click Aang for his new wooden menu.
Claude progress bars move the instant Claude does.
Claude bars learn real times and show stalls.
Aang answers sooner, and his replies flow in smoothly.
Samara's tab list is bigger and easier to read, with a small x to close a tab.
Closing Samara also closes the pop-out playing its tab.
Twitch in the pop-out catches up to live after an ad, so sound and picture match.
One broom tidies both your tabs and Claude's mockups.
Labels and links in Samara are easier to read.
On your Mac, mockups Claude makes now open in Samara's Mockups trail.
Claude on your Mac now knows: mockups always go to Samara.
On your Mac, Notes for this site is hidden for now; your notes live with Aang on the PC.
Samara opens much faster, even the first time each day.
Pages come back where you left them, no jump.
Dark pages no longer flash white when Samara opens.
Letting ads through on a site now really works.
Keyboard sites like Epomaker can connect, once you say yes.
Closing the pop-out puts the video straight back in Samara.
The first pop-out opens as fast as the rest.
On your Mac, Samara fades aside for the pop-out instead of shrinking into the Dock.
The tab list slides out smoothly the first time too.
With two keyboards plugged in, Samara asks which one, like Chrome.
The tab list arrow turns over as the list slides; closing eases in.
Bookmarks get the site's real icon more often, not just a letter.
Sites with only a fancy icon still get their real icon on bookmarks.
Pick Small, Medium or Large tabs in Settings, for each computer.
The broom no longer sits on top of your tabs.
The Settings tab wears Samara's lantern.
The search bar is bigger, steadier and remembers your searches.
Click the search bar to see recent searches and sites.
ALL MOCKUPS in the trail opens your quest log.
Samara keeps your data yours, the way Brave does.
Samara updates itself from GitHub on both computers.
Every version always lists the version you are on.
